finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. Its only check is a substring match for "example.io" on the raw string, so any URL that contains that text passes. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. Examples: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/cdn#example.io, http://example.io.attacker.com/, http://attacker.com/example.io. The scheme and host are not restricted and redirects are followed by default.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) (main.go:36), with the response body streamed to the client via io.Copy (main.go:38)

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") reads the attacker-controlled value
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation. It is a substring check on the raw string, not a parsed host check, so it is trivially satisfied
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP or host restrictions
The response is reflected to the attacker, so internal and metadata responses are readable

finding.guards_checked: Only the strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") check at line 32. It does not parse the URL, check the host or scheme, or resolve to an IP, and it is not an allowlist. There is no redirect restriction, no egress filtering and no authentication in the handler.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, not a closing guard). The strict hostname allowlist is in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20), not /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 reads attacker-controlled `logo`, main.go:32 only does a substring check, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 copies the body back, so full-read SSRF is possible. No auth or middleware exists in this file (main.go:41-44).
